Subject: Subprocessor exposure for EU pilot — temporary processors and residency questions

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. As we scope the EU pilot, our legal/compliance team needs a short declaration of any temporary or transit subprocessors that might be involved in the path for telemetry, observability, or CDN edge caching. Specifically: 

- A one-page inventory of subprocessors handling customer data (roles + countries).
- Any temporary/transient processors that might be used during burst/beta (names, exposure window).
- Clarify where KV/prefix caches and logs are stored and whether they cross EU borders.

We don't need full SOC artifacts yet — this is for our intake team to sign off on the pilot. If you have a copy of the latest subprocessor inventory and a simple dataflow diagram, that would be perfect. Can you turn this around by Friday (7/21)?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Clara D'Souza
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
ClearBay Systems

PS: attaching our intake template in case it helps (not attached here).

Quick responses inline: 
- We can provide a one-page inventory and a drawio dataflow that highlights residency and transient processors.

Ben/Kimberly — can you confirm availability to assemble the inventory + call out any temporary agents and their retention windows? If possible, attach the two artifacts Clara requested and a brief note on KMS/HSM usage for key material.

Grace / team — pulling the spreadsheet now. Notes for Clara (to be reflected in the inventory):

- Core processors: EdgeBridge (EU-only), CacheWave (EU regional PoPs), TelemetryHub (EU+US but logs routed to EU buckets for this pilot).
- Temporary/burst: Streamlyx (analytics bridge) — typical exposure window 0-48 hours; configured to use Frankfurt PoP for pilot unless otherwise requested.
- Observability: we push runtime metrics to our observability vendor (LogSight); we can redact payloads and keep only telemetry aggregates for ClearBay pilot.
- KMS: Customer data encryption keys are managed via our KMS integration; for Private/Dedicated customers we offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via HSM-backed KMS. For hosted pilots, keys are tenant-scoped and stored in EU KMS region.

I'll attach the draft inventory and a simplified dataflow diagram. Grace — if Legal wants explicit attestation wording for the temporary bridge, suggest a short addendum: "Streamlyx will be used only for ingestion bursts, retention ≤ 48 hours, access limited to ops engineers, and configured to use EU PoPs for ClearBay pilot."

Ben Carter
Sr. Product Ops Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_v1.xlsx, dataflow_edgepath_v2.drawio

1) Can you confirm whether any telemetry logs will be copied to backups in non-EU regions during normal operations (not burst)? The inventory suggests we route logs to an EU object store, but we need explicit confirmation.

2) Please confirm the availability of an HSM-backed key option for the pilot (we would prefer BYOK if feasible). If BYOK is not possible for hosted, confirm how keys are scoped and the retention/deletion process.

3) If you could provide the Streamlyx addendum language (as proposed) in a short email that we can reference in our intake — that would close out our checklist.

If you can reply by end of day Monday (7/23) it helps us keep the pilot schedule. If not, we can schedule a 20-min sync early next week.

Thanks,
